title: Monocentric analysis of open surgical treatment of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms using off-pump technique to ensure perioperative visceral and peripheral perfusion
summary: The surgical treatment of pathoogies of the thoracoabdominal aorta (TAAA) is associated with many risks, e.g. spinal cord damage, heart problems and circulatory disorders in the brain. A heart-lung machine is often used in these procedures to maintain circulation during the operation. An alternative method - the so-called ‘off pump’ technique - does without this machine and instead uses a special bypass (‘Gott shunt’) to ensure blood flow to vital organs. This method was developed back in 1988 and could be particularly helpful in emergencies and in hospitals without a heart-lung machine. The aim of this study is to use patient data to analyse how successful this off-pump method is in order to improve future treatment decisions and guidelines.
conditions: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, without mention of rupture

interventions.name: This retrospective study evaluates the off-pump technique for the open surgical treatment of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms. The primary endpoint of this study is 30-day mortality as well as the rate of peri- and post-interventional strokes and spinal ischaemia.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients with TAAA who were treated with the off-pump method in our clinic in the period from 29 January 2016 to 31 February 2025 will be included in the study
Exclusion criteria:
no further exclusion criteria
